_readme: Camera-family calibration profile bank (Task 6.3, design doc §6.3).
WHAT THIS IS FOR. Different fundus cameras produce systematically different
images: different vignetting, colour balance, resolution and aspect ratio. A
model trained mostly on one camera degrades on another -- the domain
generalization gap, and the single biggest threat to this system working
outside the lab. The PS names portable-camera image quality as a concern; this
is the answer to it.
THE THRESHOLDS BELOW ARE HAND-BUILT AND UNVALIDATED. They were chosen from
the optics of each camera class, not fitted to data, because there is no
multi-camera dataset here to fit them to. Design doc §6.3 calls for exactly
this -- a heuristic, not a trained classifier -- given how little multi-camera
data will realistically be available. Treat every boundary as a starting
point and re-derive them the moment real multi-camera images exist. Do not
quote a classification accuracy for this; none has been measured.
deviceAssociations maps the worker-reported cameraDeviceId to the family we
EXPECT that device to produce. A mismatch between reported and detected is
not an error to suppress -- it is itself a useful signal that something
unusual happened during capture (design doc §9.4).
FEATURE STRENGTH IS NOT EQUAL, and the ranges reflect that. Every feature
holds a veto, so a range that is too tight on a WEAK feature rejects images
the strong features had already identified correctly.
vignetteSharpness  STRONGEST. A property of the optics themselves, which
neither the operator nor the eye can change.
aspectRatio        Strong. Fixed by the sensor and the manufacturer's crop.
redGreenRatio      Moderate. Sensor and illuminant, but fundus pigmentation
varies between patients and pushes it around.
retinalCoverage    WEAKEST. Mostly operator framing, not optics -- a
handheld camera aimed carefully fills the frame as fully
as a tabletop one. Its range is deliberately wide; a
tight one sent a correctly-identified portable image to
'unknown' purely on how well it happened to be framed.

desktop_tabletop.description: Classic tabletop fundus camera. Large circular FOV filling most of a roughly 4:3 frame, crisp vignette edge from well-defined optics, neutral colour balance.

portable_handheld.description: Handheld portable fundus camera. Smaller FOV, softer vignette edge from simpler optics, often a warmer cast and stronger corner falloff.

smartphone_adapter.description: Phone sensor behind a lens adapter. Tall or wide phone aspect ratio, small retinal circle in a large frame, soft edge, aggressive in-camera processing.

unknown.description: No family matched. Falls back to the neutral profile -- deliberately identical to doing nothing, so an unrecognised camera is never made WORSE by a guessed correction.

_deviceAssociationsReadme: The family each WORKER-REPORTED device implies. classifyCameraFamily.m
compares it against the family it detects in the image; a disagreement is
A null value means DELIBERATELY NOT CHECKABLE -- the id names no single
camera family, so there is nothing to compare against and camera_mismatch
is stored as NULL ('nobody could check'), not false ('the two agree').
A device MISSING from this table behaves the same way at runtime, which is
why every id the PHC front-end offers is listed here explicitly: an
omission and a decision must not look identical. verify_camera_vocabulary.js
fails if captureOptions.js starts offering an id this table does not name.
